A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLOPS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding material can be matched despite restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, prompt-tuning, alignment-timing, robustness, and gradient-estimation experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds multi-query Mezo results to Table 1.

M1.justification: The Gaussian allocator, trace objective, LR optimization, and training pseudocode are retained. v3 Equation (6) explicitly restricts Bernoulli query halving to examples with below-mean clean loss. v1 gives a generic probability-p halving rule but also describes feature-conditioned allocation and pruning unimportant examples. Whether this changes the procedure or documents an existing condition is unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven image-classification datasets, CLIP prompt-tuning tasks, LCS-558K alignment task, and natural-corruption/adversarial-attack scenarios. No evaluated dataset, domain, or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Mezo (n-SPSA) for both ViT sizes alongside the existing Mezo (2 queries), DeepZero (n-SPSA), LR, OPS methods, and BP. This is an additional multi-query comparator variant; the other experiments retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes stated ViT training from 100 to 10 epochs and batch size from 64 to 128. Appendix C.1 replaces base-model query budgets of 20/60/120 and large-model budgets of 20/20/60/120 with 20 throughout; classification-head budgets fall from 60 to 20. These substantially revise the reported protocol, without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The allocator, query-budget, layer-depth, and attention-versus-FFN analyses are retained in Figure 4 and Appendix C.4. The robustness comparisons in Table 3 are also unchanged. v1 Figure 5 becomes v3 Figure 6 without new analysis.

E5.justification: The gradient-similarity plots retain the same shaded bands. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, definitions of these bands, or significance tests; no uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds two multi-query Mezo rows, including ImageNet accuracies of 54.8% for ViT-base and 56.7% for ViT-large. Existing table values and plotted findings are retained. Because the stated ViT settings change, the retained numbers do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) correct the noise-density score derivative from differentiation with respect to theta to differentiation with respect to z. v3 also supplies an explicit conditional distribution for BA. Assumption 1, both principal theorems, and their substantive appendix derivations remain the same.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit claim to be the first work to formulate query allocation for forward learning. The central optimal-allocation, theoretical-guarantee, scalability, 20-query, and forward-learning performance claims are otherwise retained.

C2.justification: v3 removes the conclusion's proposed application to nondifferentiable human-preference objectives. The remaining interpretations and limitations—including the gap to BP, variance heterogeneity, layer-dependent estimation difficulty, and attention-related memory costs—are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation-repository link in the abstract and explicitly documents BA's clean-loss threshold. It also revises the training/query-budget information identified under E3. Hardware, preprocessing, model dimensions, and prompt-tuning/alignment implementation details remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning: the swarm-focused BP-free discussion shifts toward feedback-free and dual-network learning, citing Frenkel, Journe, and Kao–Hariharan. A new paragraph distinguishes FLOPS's perturbation-noise variance from dataset-sampling variance in importance sampling and reshuffling, citing Zhao–Zhang and Lu. Several generic architecture references are removed.

P1.justification: v3 expands and retitles Section 3, separates Section 4 into allocator, optimization, and reparameterization subsections, and rewrites the conclusion and selected introductory passages. Author affiliations and conference headers also change. The overall section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised with explicit module notation and updated labels. Table 1 gains comparator rows and rearranges/highlights OPS rows. The former Figure 3 panels become separate Figures 3 and 5, prompting relocation and renumbering of later displays. Existing result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves estimator specification and research positioning, adds a multi-query Mezo comparison, and provides a code pointer. However, Section 5.1 and Appendix C.1 sharply reduce the stated training and query budgets while retaining all existing accuracies, without explaining whether these are corrections or rerun results. Since efficiency is central to the paper, this unresolved relationship between settings and evidence prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
